question: Why is it important for nurses to study both morbidity and mortality statistics together?

question: What vital information must go on the label of a freshly diluted lotion?

question: Which of the following is an early physical sign of significant blood loss?

question: What is a common health vulnerability frequently faced by single-parent households?

options.B: To run expensive blood tests on everyone every single day
options.C: To watch if they fall sick before they can spread the disease

question: How can you best describe the latent stage of conflict?

question: What was the main goal of introducing workers' compensation laws?

options.A: To fund free medical schools for aspiring occupational health nurses

question: What main factor decides if a patient develops mild (paucibacillary) or severe (multibacillary) leprosy?

options.B: The person's age when infected
options.C: The country where exposure happened

question: During a neuro exam, why do nurses check different parts of the body instead of just the head?

options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the evaluation

question: What is the main reason we tie a tourniquet before doing venepuncture?

options.C: To disinfect the skin surface before needle entry
options.D: To engorge and make the veins more visible

question: How often should an IV insertion site covered with a transparent dressing be visually inspected by the nurse?

question: A complete health assessment for an older adult looks at their physical health plus what other key areas?

question: Why is patient teaching so important when managing chronic open-angle glaucoma?

options.C: The disease is usually painless, so patients might skip lifelong treatment

question: Why is pre-training essential for nurses who will use research checklists on the ward?

question: A school clinic notices a sudden jump in waterborne infections among students. What should the team do next?

question: What is the main purpose of the HEEADSSS tool when assessing a teenager?

question: Why do some degenerative disorder patients lose weight rapidly even when they eat normal meals?

question: A pregnant patient at 32 weeks says she hasn't felt her baby kick all day. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.C: Give her a strong laxative to stimulate digestive activity
options.D: Tell her this is completely normal and send her back home

question: What is the medical term for the very first menstrual period in a young female?

question: What is the main feature of a unit dispensing system?

question: Which pregnancy hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing the valve between the stomach and food pipe?

question: What is the term for a nurse's legal obligation to answer for their professional actions?

question: Why does supine hypotension happen when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back?

question: When is a topical drug most likely to cause unexpected whole-body (systemic) side effects?

question: A nurse notices that new mothers in the postnatal ward look anxious about breastfeeding. Which option turns this into a well-focused research study?

question: A patient is prescribed liquid iron. What should the nurse teach them to prevent stained teeth?

question: What usually happens if health spending has zero government regulation or control?

question: How does stepping further away from an active X-ray source affect your radiation exposure?

question: As a nurse, what is your key responsibility when giving medications for hormone disorders?

question: Why do we perform Leopold's maneuvers when a pregnant woman is admitted?

question: Why is secondary adrenal insufficiency caused by pituitary problems so dangerous for a patient?

question: Which group is generally at the highest risk of abuse and neglect in home care settings?

question: What does a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment primarily look at?

question: What protective gear is a must-have when preparing cytotoxic drugs?

explanation: Brain herniation is a medical emergency where high pressure forces brain tissue to shift where it shouldn't go. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which eye finding is most often seen in a patient with poorly controlled high blood pressure?

options.A: Drusen under the macula
options.B: Sticky pus from the conjunctiva
options.C: Cloudy protein clumps in the lens
options.D: Flame-shaped retinal hemorrhages

explanation: You nailed it! High pressure can strain tiny retinal blood vessels until they burst, creating little flame-shaped bleeds that show up during an eye exam. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T4#GNS311_U3_T4_h7)

question: How does empowering a patient with a physical disability help them through community nursing care?

options.A: It encourages the patient to take an active role in their own healthcare decisions
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future medical or nursing supervision
options.C: It guarantees immediate employment and financial independence
options.D: It removes all environmental barriers found within the public transport system

explanation: Empowerment builds self-advocacy so patients lead the conversation about their own health instead of just sitting back. You're becoming an advocate nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h8)

question: Why do nurses check the ear canal with an otoscope after finishing an irrigation?

options.A: To check if the patient's hearing loss is permanent
options.B: To measure the exact length of the ear canal
options.C: To pump remaining air out of the middle ear space
options.D: To make sure the wax or object is actually gone

explanation: An otoscope check lets you double-check your work and confirm the ear canal is clean and the eardrum looks safe. Perfect finish! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h6)

question: What defines gestational diabetes mellitus compared to pregestational diabetes?

options.A: It is first recognized during pregnancy
options.B: It requires permanent insulin use after delivery
options.C: It causes no risk to the developing fetus
options.D: It only occurs in women over age forty

explanation: Gestational diabetes is specifically diagnosed for the first time during the pregnant state, unlike pregestational diabetes which was present before conception. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h2)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the master control center to start the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The adrenal gland
options.B: The thyroid gland
options.C: The pituitary gland
options.D: The hypothalamus

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the head office in the brain—it sends the very first signal (GnRH) to kick off the cycle! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which blood vessels have walls that are only one cell thick for easy exchange of nutrients and gases?

options.A: Capillaries
options.B: Vena cava
options.C: Arterioles
options.D: Arteries

explanation: Capillaries are the tiniest blood vessels. Because their walls are just one cell thick, oxygen and nutrients can easily slip out to feed your tissues while waste slips in. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)

question: Why do we use the nursing diagnosis 'Fatigue' for someone with anemia?

options.A: To ensure the patient stays on strict bed rest all day
options.B: To prove the patient is not sleeping well at night
options.C: To address reduced oxygen-carrying capacity in the blood
options.D: To document that the patient is refusing hospital food

explanation: Anemia means fewer red blood cells to ferry oxygen around. Less oxygen means less energy for the body—hence, deep fatigue! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which stage in the Kubler-Ross model involves a person trying to make a deal with God to change an inevitable outcome?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Denial
options.C: Bargaining
options.D: Anger

explanation: Bargaining involves trying to negotiate a different outcome or postpone the inevitable loss. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient has heavy bleeding, bad cramps, an open cervix, and reports that some tissue has passed but parts are still inside. What is this called?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Missed abortion
options.C: Incomplete abortion
options.D: Septic abortion

explanation: When some tissue comes out but part of it stays trapped inside with an open cervix, we call it an incomplete abortion. Great clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h2)

question: Your patient scheduled for a liver biopsy says they just took their morning dose of warfarin (a blood thinner). What should you do?

options.A: Tell them to walk around the ward to sweat it out
options.B: Go ahead with the test since morning doses do not matter
options.C: Inform the doctor immediately and expect the test to be delayed
options.D: Give them vitamin K right away to reverse it

explanation: You nailed it. Warfarin thins the blood and raises bleeding risks, so the doctor must be told right away so they can reschedule safely. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is the standard first-line medication for treating long-term hypothyroidism?

options.A: Levothyroxine
options.B: Propylthiouracil
options.C: Methimazole
options.D: Propranolol

explanation: Correct! Levothyroxine is a synthetic hormone that safely replaces what the natural thyroid isn't making enough of. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h5)

question: How many traditional 'rights' make up the golden rules of safe drug administration?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Seven
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

explanation: Think of the classic five: right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, and right time. Master these, and you're well on your way! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h2)
